Chapter 6: Shaping Your Environment—The Power of Surroundings and Associations
Have you ever noticed how your surroundings can quietly influence the way you think, act, and even dream?
Just like a plant thrives or withers depending on its soil and sunlight, we’re shaped by the energy, attitudes, and expectations of the people and places around us.
So, if you want to think bigger and keep moving forward, it’s worth asking—what would happen if you intentionally designed your environment to help you grow?
Here’s the simple truth: people tend to rise—or fall—to the level of their environment.
When you spend most of your time with folks who are negative, complacent, or who dismiss ambition, it gets tough to stay motivated and enthusiastic.
But what if you surrounded yourself with people who are optimistic, proactive, and genuinely supportive? Suddenly, your spirits lift, and your horizons start to expand.
So, how do you shape an environment that really fuels your growth? Here are a few practical steps you can take:
First, seek out relationships with people who inspire you, challenge you, and encourage your progress.
Next, try to limit your time with those who constantly reinforce doubt, cynicism, or small thinking.
You can also create physical spaces—at home or at work—that are organized, uplifting, and make it easier to focus.
And don’t forget to regularly expose yourself to new ideas—maybe through books, podcasts, events, or even travel.
Let’s say you’re dreaming of starting your own business. Imagine joining a local entrepreneur group, attending workshops, or finding a mentor who’s already walked that path.
These kinds of connections bring more than just advice or resources—they give you a real sense of belonging and shared purpose.
There’s something else to keep in mind, too. Our cultural norms and expectations can have a subtle but powerful influence on what we believe is possible for us.
Sometimes, the biggest thing holding us back is the fear of standing out or being judged.
That’s why it makes such a difference to find—or build—communities that celebrate ambition and learning.
When you do, you give yourself permission to reach for bigger goals.
Remember, shaping your environment isn’t a one-time project—it’s an ongoing process. As your ambitions grow, so should the quality and diversity of your influences.
And that naturally leads us to what’s next: building positive relationships and mastering the art of encouragement.
